sheet-79.description: The western half of the village of Oceanic, now part of Rumson borough, drawn at 60 feet to an inch. The sheet runs from the shore of the North Shrewsbury River at the top down past Main Street to the blocks south of South or Church Street, and from beyond 3rd Avenue on the left to Allen Street at the right edge, where it meets sheet 80. Main and South or Church Street cross the sheet from left to right; 3rd, 2nd and 1st Avenues and Allen run up the page towards the river, and a short Lane joins 3rd and 2nd Avenues north of Main. The upper left is taken up by the M.C.D. Borden green houses, a large private range of glass-roofed houses drawn in pink around two ponds, with a heaters' basement. The rest is a residential village of frame dwellings, mostly of one and a half to three stories, set in deep lots, with a row of small stores (one of them hay and grain) on Main Street between 2nd and 1st Avenues, a barber and a post office near Allen, and a small green-coloured shop building behind the Main Street lots. At the upper right, beside the river, a corner of the Oceanic Inn and its platform reaches in from the next sheet. A panel under the village name gives the population as 800, prevailing winds west, water facilities as in the Long Branch report, and the fire equipment: no steam or hand engine, one independent hose cart with 500 feet of hose, one chemical engine and one hook and ladder truck. An 18 inch water pipe runs along Main Street. Large lots south of Main between 3rd and 2nd Avenues and west of 3rd Avenue are open ground.
notes: Main is today's West River Road; South or Church is Church Street; 3rd, 2nd and 1st Avenues are 3rd, 2nd and 1st Streets; Allen is Allen Street.
The Lane between 3rd and 2nd Avenues is taken to be today's William Street at its 2nd Street end; 3rd Avenue north of Main does not follow modern 3rd Street, so that junction was left out.
M.C.D. Borden green houses (private) occupy the upper left block.
Village panel: population 800; one independent hose cart, one chemical engine and one hook and ladder truck; no steam or hand engine.

sheet-80-1.description: The centre of the village of Oceanic, now part of Rumson borough, drawn at 60 feet to an inch. The part runs from Hunt Street at the top down past Main Street to the blocks south of South or Church Street, and from Allen Street at the left edge, where sheet 79 joins, across Lafayette, Washington and Bingham Avenues to open land east of Bingham. The lower right corner of the sheet is a separate inset and is not part of this area. Along Main Street stand the village's public and commercial buildings: the Lafayette House with a saloon, a barber, the fire department house (hose cart, hook and ladder truck, chemical engine), a coal yard and office, the Oceanic M.E. Church, a blacksmith and a meat market. The First Presbyterian Church stands in the large block between Washington and Bingham Avenues north of Main, and the public school, heated by hot air, is in the block between Allen and Lafayette south of Main. Red Men's Hall is on South or Church Street at Lafayette Avenue, and a boys' club is on Washington Avenue. At the top left the Oceanic Inn with its saloon and landing platform sits on the river shore. The rest is frame dwellings and outbuildings in deep lots, with a windmill and a building foundation north of Main. East of Bingham Avenue the blocks are largely empty and marked no exposure. A 4 inch water pipe runs up Washington Avenue and an 18 inch pipe along Main Street.
notes: Main is today's West River Road west of Bingham Avenue and East River Road east of it; South or Church is Church Street; Lafayette and Washington Avenues are Lafayette and Washington Streets; Hunt is Hunt Street.
Buildings of note: Oceanic Inn, Lafayette House, fire department, Oceanic M.E. Church, First Presbyterian Church, public school, Red Men's Hall, boys' club.
The block east of Bingham Avenue is marked no exposure.

Printed sheet 80, Scale 60 ft to an inch. Oceanic centre: Main (West/East River Road) and South or Church Street crossed by Allen, Lafayette, Washington and Bingham Avenues, Hunt Street at top. Two parts: main map, and an inset at lower right of Washington Avenue from Hunt Street north to the Iron Bridge over the North Shrewsbury River (Lenox, Shrewsbury Inn).

sheet-80-2.description: An inset in the lower right corner of sheet 80, drawn at 60 feet to an inch and at the same orientation as the main map, showing Washington Avenue north of Hunt Street, beyond the top edge of the main map, as far as the North Shrewsbury River. The avenue reaches the river at the Iron Bridge, which carries it across the water; the shore is drawn in blue across the inset. Between Hunt Street and the river are two blocks. On the west side of Washington Avenue stand The Lenox, a two and a half story hotel or boarding house, and several dwellings, with vacant land beyond; on the east side is the Shrewsbury Inn, a three story building with a shed, and a large building at the Hunt Street corner that is also drawn at the top of the main map. A 4 inch water pipe runs up Washington Avenue. Below Hunt Street the inset repeats a strip of the main map. The sheet scale bar and the lower part of the compass rose are drawn just above the inset border.
notes: Placed from one detected junction (Hunt Street / Washington Street) with the scale and rotation of the main map; low confidence along the avenue towards the river.
Washington Avenue crossed the river by the Iron Bridge; today's Oceanic Bridge crosses from the foot of Bingham Avenue instead.
Buildings of note: The Lenox, Shrewsbury Inn.
